appearance_facts.fact: Chart title reads 'Product Rating Share by Category'. Plot area spans roughly x=270-1860, y=300-1560.
Six category markers left-to-right: Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other.
Quality marker near (450,840); Price near (690,735); Design near (935,410); Support near (1180,930); Delivery near (1425,625); Other near (1670,690).
All six markers are identical blue filled circles with dark outlines; vertical position encodes the Value axis, not the printed % label.
Design circle sits highest on the Value axis (~54); Support circle sits lowest (~30).
Printed % labels do not match marker height: Design's label (34%) is on the highest marker, while Other's label (53%) is on a mid-height marker.

printed_facts.fact: Axis label 'Category'; tick labels Quality, Price, Design, Support, Delivery, Other.
Quality = 36%; Price = 38%; Design = 34%; Support = 45%; Delivery = 43%; Other = 53%.

Option labels are Select Other, Select Design, Select Support; policy table states decision metric 'mislabeled_value / labeled rating share' and rule 'Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share'.

public_definitions: Promotion budget rule: Select the category with the highest current labeled rating share
Decision metric: mislabeled_value / labeled rating share
chart_reference: Use the dashboard labeled rating-share values as the evidence source; the promotion budget is reserved for the category with the strongest current rating-share signal.
uncertain: The printed % labels conflict with the marker heights on the Value axis (e.g., Design label 34% on the tallest marker; Other label 53% on a mid marker), so 'labeled rating share' is taken from the printed % text, not the y-position.
Among the three selectable options (Other, Design, Support), the printed labels are Other 53%, Design 34%, Support 45%; the full-chart maximum printed label is Other 53%.
